name: Longer Laser B1 30W
tagline: 30W Longer's large-format diode: bigger bed than Ray5 for sign-sized projects
tldr: Longer Laser B1 30W is the 30W SKU on the Longer longer laser b1 line. Longer's large-format B1 20W diode: this profile is the 20W SKU only; Longer also sells 30W and 40W B1 machines separately. Verify optical power on the listing: do not assume combined-watt marketing.
mainObjective: Faster cutting and deeper hobby cuts while keeping solid engraving capability

priceRange.note: 30W optical module: verify SKU before buying

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Keeps the fine 0.08 × 0.1 mm spot of the entry module while cutting faster
Fills at ~39–88 mm/s: a 10 × 10 cm photo in ~14–22 min
Basic set at $569.99 on Longer's store (October 2026)
cons: Gains are moderate in our benchmarks: a 3 mm square still takes ~7–12 min
The Pro Max set ($949.99) costs more than the stronger B1 in basic trim
Longer's 20 mm one-pass claim is far beyond our cut benchmark
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 30W SKU on Longer Laser B1. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Tune cut passes with air assist and focus checks. For photo engraving, slow down vs your cut presets: this head is optimized for throughput on wood, not only finesse.
primaryUse: Cut-biased diode tier for makers who outgrew 10–20W job times but stay on the same frame

editorialDepth.advantages: Longer Laser B1 30W targets mixed engraving and wood-cutting weeks: fewer passes on basswood and dark acrylic than weaker SKUs in the same line.
editorialDepth.limitations: Wrong pick if you never engrave and only wanted the lowest price. Ultra-fine photo work can look better on an engraving-first SKU. Open-frame: safety and smoke are on you.

faq.question: What does the B1 30W cut in one pass?
faq.answer: Longer's spec sheet claims 20 mm basswood in one pass and 50 mm acrylic maximum. In our benchmarks a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood takes about 7–12 min at 3–7 mm/s; around 8 mm basswood and 5 mm dark acrylic are realistic in passes.

faq.question: Is the 30W the sensible middle of the B1 range?
faq.answer: Often, yes. It keeps the same 0.08 × 0.1 mm spot as the 20W, so engraving detail is unchanged, while cutting and filling faster. Its basic set was $90 more than the 20W and $130 less than the 40W on Longer's store in October 2026.

faq.question: Which B1 30W bundle makes sense?
faq.answer: Longer listed the Basic set at $569.99, the Pro set at $729.99, the Pro Max set at $949.99 and the Basic set with IR module at $929.99 (October 2026). At Pro Max prices, the 40W basic set ($699.99) becomes a serious alternative if cutting is your priority.

standoutFeatures.title: Speed without losing detail
standoutFeatures.body: Same 0.08 × 0.1 mm spot as the entry B1, with fills about two to three times faster in our tests.

standoutFeatures.title: 450 × 440 mm bed
standoutFeatures.body: Room for sign-sized panels, with the same extension kit as the rest of the B1 range.
